## Correction: failure evidence does not mutate the remote ledger
This supersedes the phrase “ledger upsert” in the earlier failure-propagation note. The canonical execution ledger remains the submission, reservation, retry-authorization, and attempt-binding record. Scheduler/accounting and attempt markers remain authoritative for a terminal job error.

The persistent observer and passive recovery are remote-read-only: they read the attempt binding from the ledger, capture exact scheduler/marker evidence, and atomically persist only the local journal event/checkpoint. They do not update ledger state or commit campaign workspace history.

An explicit attached `campaign status --refresh` or future separately authorized reconciliation command reads a pinned source state, projects a material failure into the campaign workspace snapshot, and creates a CAS-protected campaign-history revision. It records FAILED only for the matching attempt; artifacts and validation remain separate. A late observation for an old attempt stays historical and cannot alter a replacement. If no explicit reconciliation has occurred, attached views label the workspace projection stale relative to local observation rather than inventing an update.

A retry still requires explicit authorization and an explicit apply after reconciliation. Neither journal observation nor recovery can consume that authorization.
